score_rationale: Exceptionally strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: at least 5 major vendors (InfoGlobalData, Blue Mail Media, AverickMedia, InsuranceAgentLists.com, ExactData) currently selling insurance agent databases ranging from 181K to 1.2M+ records with pricing starting at $0.15/record (typical 100K list = $15,000). Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) insurance carriers recruiting agents for distribution networks — each recruited agent generates $50K-$200K/year in premium volume, making recruiting database spend trivial; (2) insurance technology vendors (CRM, quoting software, agency management systems, lead generation platforms) selling $500-$5,000/year SaaS subscriptions to agents; (3) continuing education (CE) providers selling mandatory state-required courses — all agents must complete 20-40 hours of CE every 1-3 years depending on state, creating recurring $200-$800/year spend per agent; and (4) financial services companies (investment advisors, mortgage brokers, tax preparers) building cross-referral partnerships with agents who serve overlapping client bases. All 50 states plus DC maintain public insurance agent license registries via their State Departments of Insurance, accessible through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR) or individual state DOI websites, with data including agent name, license number, status (active/inactive), license type (Life & Health, Property & Casualty, both), issue/renewal dates, resident state, and affiliated agency/carrier. Zero PII — all professional credential data under state insurance codes. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 51 state insurance department websites (many states offer bulk downloads or API access), deduplicate multi-state license holders, normalize agency affiliations, and enrich with license type flags. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions ($2,000-$10,000/year) or per-record pricing ($0.15-$0.50/record), leaving a clear gap for a one-time $99-$149 CSV. Audience size is massive: over 1.2 million licensed insurance agents nationwide, creating a TAM of 15,000+ potential B2B buyers (insurance carriers, software vendors, CE providers, recruiting firms). Score is 9 due to validated exceptionally high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors at premium pricing ($0.15/record baseline), confirmed public data availability across all states with NIPR aggregation, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives, massive agent population (1.2M+), and four distinct B2B buyer segments with proven high-LTV purchasing behavior.

Each record includes the agent's full name, license number(s), license status (active, inactive, expired, suspended), license type(s) held (Life & Health, Property & Casualty, Personal Lines, or combined), original issue date, current expiration/renewal date, resident state, non-resident states (where applicable), affiliated agency name or carrier, and city/state of practice. Financial advisors, mortgage brokers, and tax professionals use agent lists to build cross-referral partnerships with agents serving overlapping client bases (small business owners, high-net-worth individuals). A one-time $99-$149 CSV undercuts annual subscription vendors by 90%+ while targeting the same B2B buyer segments.

data_wanted: All 50 state Departments of Insurance (DOI) plus DC maintain public insurance agent license registries, accessible via state-specific DOI websites or aggregated through the National Insurance Producer Registry (NIPR). No authentication required for lookup (though some states may require scraping vs. bulk download or API access). Key fields per license: agent full name (first, middle initial, last), license number (format varies by state, typically 8-12 alphanumeric characters), license status (active, inactive, expired, suspended, revoked), license type(s) held (Life & Health, Property & Casualty, Personal Lines, or combined — many agents hold multiple types), original issue date, current expiration or renewal date, resident state (agent's primary licensing state), non-resident states (where agent also holds reciprocal licenses), affiliated agency name or insurance carrier (availability varies by state; independent agents may list agency DBA, captive agents list carrier), practice address city and state (some states list full street address, others only city/state), and appointment status with specific carriers (where publicly listed). Target all active and inactive-but-not-revoked licenses (exclude only revoked, surrendered, or fraud-suspended). Scope to individual agents only — exclude agency business entities (which have separate entity registrations). Approximately 1.2 million active insurance agent licenses nationwide as of 2026 (note: multi-state license holders mean unique individual count is ~800K-900K). Target output: 1.2M rows, one per license (some individuals appear multiple times if licensed in multiple states). Data is 100% public per state insurance statutes (professional licensing records are public information under state Freedom of Information laws and NAIC model regulations).
